basis: Benign tumour arising in the adrenal medulla, an endocrine gland.
Substance-related withdrawal umbrella; transient neurologic and autonomic symptoms do not establish common organ damage. Delirium and seizures are not universal.
Localized loss of subcutaneous fat defines the disease; systemic metabolic dysfunction is not characteristic.
Severe Zellweger disease: brain and liver dysfunction usually >80%; renal cortical cysts commonly >30%. Skeletal, ocular and hearing abnormalities omitted at the four-axis cap.
Inherited renal tubulopathy defined by Gitelman-like electrolyte wasting and metabolic alkalosis; mitochondrial inheritance alone adds no other organ.
Congenital hypoplasia or absence of the femur.
Defining marrow hypoplasia, neutropenia, monocytopenia and congenital deafness; deficient innate immunity causes recurrent bacterial infections.
Familial primary hyperparathyroidism; skeletal demineralization affects >30% over the course. Renal stones are separately diagnosed; jaw tumours are not universal.
Necrotizing phlegmonous gastritis is a bacterial infection of the gastric wall progressing to gangrene.
Benign tumour of a major salivary gland; salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Endocrine deficiencies and polyneuropathy define the syndrome. Progressive hearing loss and alopecia each occur in 30-79%; weakness and pes cavus reflect neuropathy.
Active peptic ulceration damages gastric or duodenal mucosa; an infectious cause is not intrinsic to every case.
Congenital skeletal myopathy with fractures; obstructive sleep apnea in 3/3 supports chronic upper-airway dysfunction. Motor delay reflects muscle disease.
Organic acid metabolism defect; developmental delay 20/20 and arrhythmias 30-79% support involvement. Cardiomyopathy <30%; hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
Immune-mediated photodermatosis; chronic cheilitis affects ~60-70% and chronic conjunctivitis ~40%, sometimes with scarring. Renal disease is not established as common.
Follicular keratosis with skin atrophy and hair loss; absent eyelashes are hair involvement, without established common ocular damage.
Congenital obstruction of the aortic valve; ventricular hypertrophy remains within the cardiovascular axis. Dyspnea alone adds no pulmonary involvement.
Defined by corneal stromal dystrophy and opacities, even though vision is usually preserved.
Thrombosis occupies a dural venous sinus. Raised-pressure symptoms alone do not establish brain damage in >=30%; cerebral infarction is a minority complication.
Broad chromosome 15 umbrella dominated by neurodevelopmental syndromes, including Angelman, Prader-Willi and ring 15; no additional organ consistently qualifies across the group.
Corneal stromal lipid deposition causes progressive visual impairment; associated systemic dyslipidemia is not intrinsic organ involvement.
Fibronectin deposition directly damages glomeruli, causing proteinuria and renal insufficiency. Hypertension and acidosis are secondary complications.
Inherited vesicoureteral reflux affects the urinary tract. Urinary infections are separate diseases rather than intrinsic infectious involvement.
Infectious abscess within the vitreous, classified as purulent endophthalmitis.
Developmental dental anomaly producing an accessory enamel-dentine cusp; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
